summary: Witchstone is a Reiner Knizia network-and-tile game where players extend paths of witches out from their towers around a central hexagonal board, scooping crystals from a shared cauldron and racing to claim scoring tiles before others. It plays with the clean, mathematical tension typical of Knizia designs, where timing and route efficiency matter more than direct confrontation.
praised: clean, elegant Knizia-style rules with real depth
satisfying network-building puzzle on the hex board
good tension from competing for the same scoring opportunities
quick to teach relative to its strategic depth
criticised: can feel dry or abstract despite the fantasy theme
route-blocking can feel harsh to newer players
less table talk or direct interaction than the fantasy theme might suggest

interaction.detail: Players extend witch paths across a shared hex board and compete for the same crystals, prophecy scrolls, and scoring tiles, so claiming a spot can block or slow a rival's route, even though each player also tracks their own private cauldron and score.

scoring.why: Scoring draws from several separate systems — the cauldron/crystals, the pentagram, prophecy scrolls, and network connections — characteristic of Knizia's multi-track point designs.
scoring.how_you_win: Move your witches to collect crystals, build spell networks, and fulfill prophecy scroll conditions, finishing with the highest total across these combined scoring tracks.
